content: {"summary":"In November 2025 node search‑cluster‑02 ran out of root disk because an unrotated OpenSearch log grew to fill the 40 GB volume. The fix is to add/restore the logrotate configuration with copytruncate and run logrotate, then verify free space.","likely_cause":"Missing logrotate configuration caused the /var/log/opensearch/*.log file to grow unchecked and fill the root disk.","confidence":"high","claims":[{"text":"A single OpenSearch log file grew to ~29 GB and filled the root disk","evidence_ids":["INC-0101#0","INC-0101#2"],"quote":"one `*.log` file under `/var/log/opensearch/` at about 29 GB"},{"text":"The node lacked a logrotate entry for OpenSearch logs, so the file was never rotated","evidence_ids":["INC-0101#1","RB-008#1"],"quote":"no OpenSearch entry in `/etc/logrotate.d/`"},{"text":"The log grew about 1 GB per day, matching the period from rebuild to full disk","evidence_ids":["INC-0101#2"],"quote":"The log grows about 1 GB a day"},{"text":"Runbook RB‑008 directs to identify large files, ensure logrotate exists, and run logrotate -f","evidence_ids":["RB-008#0","RB-008#1"],"quote":"run `sudo logrotate -f /etc/logrotate.d/<name>`"}],"next_checks":["Verify that logrotate files for /var/log/opensearch/*.log exist on all search‑cluster nodes (-01, -02, -03)","Confirm that the copytruncate option is set so OpenSearch keeps logging after rotation","Check that the 90% /var alert is assigned an owner and escalated promptly","Monitor /var usage after cleanup to ensure space remains available"]}
